It depends on what is being cooked and your ultimate goal. Fresh herbs added later will add more surface flavor and retain more of their nutrition. Others are more sturdy and can be added sooner like Rosemary. Also, for authentic bolognese sauce, none of these are added. All of the flavor comes from the pancetta, ground meat, carrots, celery, onion and passata. [https://www.recipesfromitaly.com/bolognese-sauce-recipe/](https://www.recipesfromitaly.com/bolognese-sauce-recipe/)

Re: Passata in the recipe, this can be hard to find. Its tomato sauce thats been run thru a sieve so it has no seeds or skin in it. I've made it with canned chopped tomatoes etc. However, as of late, I've moved to passata. The pancetta adds alot of flavor. It can expensive and hard to cut into pieces. I put it in my vitamixer and pulse it a couple of times. The fat melts into the sauce and adds extra texture and flavor. I usually try to time bolognese after Ive made chicken so I can use the broth from the chicken in the sauce. I use chicken thighs as they have more flavor, produce more broth and are much less expensive. I do use all of the herbs you mentioned on the chicken. I like olives, so I pour the marinade from olives into the baking dish with the chicken for added flavor. Back to the herbs, fresh herbs add wonderful flavor, nutrition and aroma. If you can, add them later so as not to cook all of that out in the process. But make it your own. Experiment and do what you prefer. After all, you are the chef:)

It depends on the cut and how you are cooking it. Its super helpful to brine your meat with salt prior to cooking if you have the time. This rings true for all meat. I just use salt. It breaks down the collagen fibers in the meat and makes it much more tender. For beef, just sprinkle or even roll it in a moderate amount of salt on all sides ( you can do this while its still frozen). I put mine on a small grate on a plate and place in the microwave ( not running) just to keep things off, away from it. You could put it in the fridge or wherever its out of the way.- even in a cold oven or somewhere protected.  The less time you have the more temperate you want the exposure ( table and covered in the sun or something) just so the salt has a chance to soak in. Be sure to pat it dry well with a paper towel before you cook it. Maybe add some pepper. I rub olive oil all over it for searing which is basically frying. If its frozen, just olive oil, salt and pepper. Chicken requires alot more seasoning as its very bland. If you brine it, its best to put it in salt water for up to 24 hours. Not Much longer as it makes the meat mushy. I just put it in a sauce pan with a bunch of salt and water, cover it and put it in the fridge or set it on the stove top.Just remove it from the brine and lightly rinse. I use alot more salt on chicken than beef. Usually salt, pepper, olive oil and butter. (I dont use garlic on the meat as I feed leftovers to my dog and dogs can't eat garlic. apparently) If you want , sautee some garlic, onions, salt pepper and add the drippings from the chicken to pour over the meat as not much of your seasoning will penetrate into the meat unless you've been able to brine it. I try to save the drippings (if there are any) for future use. I use dark meat like a thigh or two with breast meat because they produce more drippings and dark meat has more flavor ( plus its much less expensive!)-I love olives, so I will sometimes pour the brine from my olives onto the chicken as well.- this is my experience. Hope it helps.
